title: The Psychology of Money
summary: An essay on twenty behavioral flaws around money: underestimating luck, trying to get returns without paying for volatility, visible spending versus hidden wealth, leverage and ruin, action bias, and the primacy of patient compounding over clever strategy.

assertions.quote: A tendency to underestimate the role of luck and risk
Take the return while trying to avoid the volatility that comes along with it.

verdicts.note: Investor return-gap studies show timing and tactical strategies underperform buy-and-hold on average.

assertions.quote: managing money isn’t necessarily about what you know; it’s how you behave.

verdicts.note: Behavior-gap research supports it, but knowledge and income still matter; the examples given are anecdotes.

assertions.quote: It’s about earning pretty good returns that you can stick with for a long period of time. That’s when compounding runs wild.

verdicts.note: Long-horizon wealth is dominated by time in market; high-return strategies tend to be unrepeatable or blow up.

assertions.quote: Wealth, in fact, is what you don’t see. It’s the cars not purchased. The diamonds not bought.

verdicts.note: Millionaire-household studies show modest consumption; conspicuous spending correlates poorly with net worth.

assertions.quote: Leverage is the devil here. It pushes routine risks into something capable of producing ruin.
has attracted armies of scammers, hucksters, and truth-benders promising the moon

verdicts.note: Regulatory enforcement records show investment fraud consistently among the largest consumer-loss categories.

assertions.quote: opportunity is almost always inversely correlated with popularity

verdicts.note: Valuation and flows evidence supports mean reversion of popular assets, but momentum can persist for long stretches.

Crypto-app downloads peaked with the Bitcoin price so that 73% of users entered above $20,000 and most of them were underwater by late 2022; crowded entry near the top went with poor subsequent returns in this one asset class.

Crypto's share of dollars invested on eToro exceeded 85% at the end-2017 price peak and then collapsed with the early-2018 crash to about 20%; a single episode where peak popularity preceded a 65% drawdown.

assertions.quote: if you start taking cues from people playing a different game than you are, you are bound to be fooled

verdicts.note: Bubble episodes show late long-horizon buyers absorbing losses when momentum traders exit.

assertions.quote: people take actions that ultimately just interrupts the execution of a good plan

verdicts.note: Brokerage studies find the most active retail accounts underperform the least active after costs.
